title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
summary:
Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are.
The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine.
Participants in the study will be given the opportunity to rate responses to health questions from the app.
The aim is to improve the design and functionality of AI-powered health tools so they can deliver relevant health information that’s easier for users to understand and act on.
Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life.

title: Have your AI call my AI
summary:
Sharp lawyers have often used the fine print to win an advantage in a contract.
It’s called the fine print for a reason–you’re not supposed to read it.
Now, armed with AI, it’s significantly easier to bury arcane, unfair or unanticipated clauses in agreements, even (and especially) if we don’t expect it.
You shouldn’t sign anything until you’ve had your AI read it.
And if it’s important, have your lawyer and her AI read it too.

title: What artificial intelligence is revealing about ancient Pompeii
summary:
POMPEII – Artificial intelligence and archaeology are coming together in two new projects at Pompeii, one of the ancient world's most iconic sites.
The second allows visitors to the archaeological site to step virtually inside ancient buildings and experience them as they were 2,000 years ago.
By combining physical anthropological and archaeological evidence with volcanological data, a team from the Pompeii Archaeological Park and the University of Padua, whose Digital Cultural Heritage Laboratory is headed by Jacopo Bonetto, has recreated the escape of one of the victims.
"If used properly, AI can help revitalise classical studies by presenting the ancient world in a more immersive way," explains Gabriel Zuchtriegel, the 45-year-old director of the Pompeii Archaeological Park.

title: Expansion proposal for Brooklyn plants fuels data center fears
summary:
The owner of a pair of floating power plants near Sunset Park, Brooklyn wants to expand the facilities, prompting protests from environmentalists who fear they could be used one day to power data centers.
The Gowanus Generation Station and nearby Narrows Generation Station are peaker facilities that are only activated during periods of peak demand.
The owner of the plants, AlphaGen, submitted an expansion plan to Con Edison earlier this year, stating that it expects the company's operating permit will be extended past 2029.
“Sunset Park is not a dumping ground for dangerous energy projects,” said State Senator Andrew Gounardes, who joined a protest Thursday over the expansion plans.
We demand investments that move us forward and we won’t stop fighting until we get them.”AlphaGen’s expansion proposal “recognizes the realities of current power technology and the need to balance reliability with sustainability,” Curt Morgan, CEO of AlphaGen said in a press release.
